div.head: III Atr 5
div.ab: And gif hwa borhleas órf habbe ⁊ landrícan hit befón, agife þæt órf ⁊ gilde XX oran.
Et si quis habeat pecus sine plegio, et tunc dominus hoc percipiat, reddat ipsum pecus et emendet uiginti oris.
And gif hwa borhleas órf habbe ⁊ landrícan hit befón, agife þæt órf ⁊ gilde XX oran.
Und wenn jemand unverbürgtes Vieh hat, und die Immunitätsherren nehmen das in Beschlag, liefere er das Vieh [ihnen] aus und büsse 20 Ör.
And if anyone has cattle without surety, and the lords of the immunity seize it, let him hand over the cattle [to them] and pay 20 ores.
And if anyone has livestock acquired without surety, and manorial lords attach it, he shall give up the livestock and pay 20 ores.
And if anyone has cattle without surety, and the lords of the estate attach it, he is to give up the cattle and pay 20 ores.

Inhaber wird nicht als Dieb, sondern als gegen Kautel des Handels (s. d. Gl 8h) Ungehorsamer bestraft
The holder is punished not as a thief but as disobedient to the safeguards of trade (see that word in Gl 8h)
According to I Atr 3³: without warranty-sureties

Falls in H gegen Q und I Atr der Plural richtig, so ist doch nur gemeint: der jedesmalige Grundherr je des Viehbesitzers. Wahrscheinlicher aber verlas H die Endvokale -a und -ó als -ā und -ō, d. i. -an, -on

If the plural in H, against Q and I Atr, is correct, then all that is meant is the respective landlord of each owner of the cattle. It is more probable, however, that H misread the final vowels -a and -ó as -ā and -ō, i.e. -an, -on
percipere in Q meint wohl nichts anderes als capere, wie er I Atr 3, 1 übersetzt
percipere in Q probably means nothing other than capere, the word he uses in translating I Atr 3, 1

In IV Eg 11 und I Atr erfolgt die Beschlagnahme zunächst nur als Sequester zugunsten des Bestohlenen, falls der sich melde. Hier ist von solcher Rückgabe an letzteren keine Rede: das Vieh wird eingezogen als gesetzwidrig erworben

In IV Eg 11 and I Atr the seizure is at first only a sequestration on behalf of the man robbed, should he come forward. Here there is no mention of any such restitution to the latter: the cattle are confiscated as unlawfully acquired

Q has dominus hoc percipiat; cf. I Atr. 3, 1. The use of the plural in the A.S. text is curious. Liebermann suggests that it may be due to a misreading of the end vowels -a and -o as -ā and -ō, i.e. as -an and -on.
Cf. I Atr. 3, 1. In IV Edg. 11 the offence is aggravated by a false oath.
